subject: Re: AtlasCloud — Order Form redlines re: output & training
messages:
From: Sasha Li <sasha.li@atlascloud.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Geller <tom.geller@atlascloud.com>, legal@atlascloud.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AtlasCloud redlines — Order Form (IP + training)

Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Please find attached a marked-up Order Form from our procurement team. Two high-level asks from legal that are blocking signature:

1) We need explicit language that AtlasCloud retains title to all Customer Output (definitions and examples attached).
2) AtlasCloud must opt-out of any training or model improvement uses of our content — no rights to use prompts/outputs/feedback for model training or improvement without separate written consent.

We appreciate Redwood's position on telemetry and product improvement, so we included a proposed narrow feedback license (Section 7.4) that preserves aggregate telemetry but excludes product-specific prompts and outputs. If Redwood can't accept the training opt-out in the Order Form we need clear mitigation steps (e.g., separate enclave, private deployment, or contractual carveout).

Attached: AtlasCloud_OrderForm_redlines.pdf (redlines), and a short extract of the clauses we changed. We'll also need an evidence list for procurement: SOC2 report and data flow diagram.

Can you confirm receipt and let us know expected turnaround on counter language?

— Sasha Li
Sasha Li
Sr. Legal Operations
AtlasCloud

- Accept customer ownership of generated output (yes/no / suggested language)
- Narrow feedback license vs. blanket training opt-out — what compromises preserve product telemetry while addressing customer risk?
- Any operational gating (Dedicated/Private options) we should propose if we can't accept their default?

I attached their pdf. Quick responses appreciated — we should get back to them within 48 hours.

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasCloud redlines — Order Form (IP + training)

Ben — thanks for the ping. High-level guidance below; I'll draft suggested language.

1) Customer Output: we can agree to a Customer Output carveout that gives AtlasCloud ownership of "Customer Generated Output" where the output is produced solely from AtlasCloud-provided prompts and data and not derived from Redwood proprietary prompts or model prompts. Suggested definition: "Customer Output" means text, files, or artifacts produced by the Service in response to Customer Input under the Agreement, excluding model weights and underlying model improvements. We should keep a Royalty-free, non-exclusive clause that allows Redwood to store and serve Customer Output for the term of the agreement (operational use) but not use it for model training.

2) Training/Feedback: we should avoid a total ban on telemetry/aggregate signals. Propose two buckets: (a) Production telemetry and performance metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) — Redwood may use in aggregate, non-identifiable form; (b) Customer-provided prompts and generated outputs — not used for training without explicit opt-in. To operationalize, add a clause allowing Redwood to request opt-in for targeted research with separate DPA/Amendment.

3) Operational mitigation: if customer requires stricter guarantees, offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with a contractual assurance that data will not leave their tenancy — this is higher-cost but acceptable.

I'll prepare redline text for the Order Form: two short replacement paragraphs for the IP/feedback sections and a fallback table listing deployment options and expected timelines. Draft ETA: end of day tomorrow.

-Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasCloud redlines — Order Form (IP + training)

Monica — adding practical negotiation points based on risk:

- Accepting Customer Output ownership is low risk provided we explicitly carve out model artifacts and any anonymized telemetry used solely for platform improvements. Must ensure Exhibit A (definitions) is precise.
- For the feedback/training clause, include a short exception enabling Redwood to use anonymous, aggregated metrics for product improvements (explicitly excludes prompts/outputs). Avoid any language that permits indefinite retention of raw prompts.
- Procurement asked for SOC2 and dataflow — provide SOC2 Type II PDF and a sanitized high-level dataflow diagram. Add the evidence-request-checklist.xlsx to the packet and offer a non-prod teleconference with our security team if needed.

Also recommend we propose a middle-ground clause: "Customer may opt-out of Training; Redwood may retain aggregated, non-identifying telemetry and may request limited, time-bound opt-in for research with prior written consent." That should be acceptable to AtlasCloud procurement.

I'll review Monica's draft and add clean contract redlines.

-Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Sasha Li <sasha.li@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Tom Geller <tom.geller@atlascloud.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasCloud redlines — Order Form (IP + training)

Sasha — thanks for the marked-up Order Form. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromise that we think meets AtlasCloud's risk needs while allowing Redwood to operate and improve the service:

1) Customer Output: Redwood will assign to AtlasCloud ownership of "Customer Output" as defined in the attached redline, limited to artifacts generated exclusively from AtlasCloud-provided inputs and not derived from Redwood proprietary prompts or longitudinal model data. This excludes model weights, training datasets, and low-level artifacts necessary to serve the model.

2) Training / Feedback: Redwood will not use Customer-provided prompts, Customer Output, or other Customer Content for model training or improving model weights without explicit, written opt-in from AtlasCloud. Redwood may retain and use aggregated, non-identifying telemetry (e.g., latency, token counts, anonymized error rates) for product improvement. We propose a short feedback license allowing Redwood to use sanitized, aggregated signals for engineering metrics only; any research uses require a separate amendment.

3) Evidence & deployment options: Attached are our SOC2 Type II and a high-level dataflow diagram. If AtlasCloud requires full data tenancy guarantees, we can provide Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private — pricing/timeline attached.

If this is acceptable, we'll circulate an updated Order Form and send via DocuSign for signature. ETA to have the redline (clean + tracked) to you by end of day tomorrow.

Links/attachments: hubspot:HS-498213, AtlasCloud_OrderForm_redlines.pdf, evidence-request-checklist.xlsx, https://www.docusign.com/EnvelopeID=3f7a9c

Next steps: please confirm AtlasCloud's acceptance of the compromise or flag any specific wording you'd like changed. Happy to set a quick call with Monica/Laura if it helps.

Best,
Ben Carter

1) In the Customer Output definition please insert "excluding content synthesized from Redwood proprietary prompts or Redwood-provided templates" for clarity.
2) For the telemetry carveout, add a 12‑month data-retention limit for aggregated signals used for product improvement.

If Redwood OKs those two tweaks we'll countersign. We also confirm receipt of the SOC2 doc and dataflow.

Thanks — Sasha
